summary:
Lesson from the FS-GG/.github#4710 installed-C runs (records templates/wasm-installed-c-run-39858275028 and templates/wasm-installed-c-run-39874053570). Each admission there buys exactly one dispatch: no re-run, a reset PR afterwards, and a failure is accepted as evidence.

- Run 1 spent its admission at the first real restore. Fixture executors had never run the caller's real restore argv, so the first hosted execution of that setup code was also its first test. A local NU1403 had earlier been dismissed as cache noise.
- Run 2 spent its admission on a race that a fast local rehearsal (24 CPUs) had hidden: Firefox's cold module-Worker boot against a fixed 250 ms policy deadline. FS.GG.Game#727 fixed it (record game/wasm-worker-startup-bound).

Practice adopted since, before asking for an admission for code that has never run hosted:
1. Run the caller's exact setup commands from clean caches with the official SDK, in a fresh container at the hosted paths. Keep that as an always-run PR control (Templates installed-c-restore-control.yml).
2. Run the full journey locally under a hosted-like CPU limit. The run-3 rehearsal used 4 CPUs by affinity.
3. Rehearse against the published package bytes that the admission names, not a local pack. The source can change between the rehearsal and the release (#4710 comments 6359687071, 6359693961, 6359765777).
4. Treat an unexplained restore or lock error as a finding until it is disproved.

A rehearsal is not a dispatch or an admission, and it proves nothing about hosted facts: runner image, mirrors, custody and timing still belong to the admitted run. The same discipline covers Home privileged scripts: rehearse probes and rollback on a scratch copy before a live cutover (github/admitted-privileged-script-lessons).

Limits: process guidance only. Each run still needs its own admission.
title: Rehearse never-hosted setup locally from clean caches, at hosted-like limits and on published bytes, before spending a single-use admission
